title: Heron's Formula
description: Class 9 IMO — Heron's Formula: finding a triangle's area from its three sides, areas of equilateral and isosceles triangles, and splitting quadrilaterals into triangles.

topics.title: Heron's Formula
topics.concept:
What is Heron's Formula?

Heron's formula (also called Hero's formula) is a method to find the area of a triangle when you know the lengths of all three sides. It is named after Hero of Alexandria, a Greek mathematician who lived around 60 CE.

Why Heron's Formula?

  • The standard formula (Area = ½ × base × height) requires knowing the height of the triangle
  • For many triangles (especially scalene triangles), finding the height is difficult
  • Heron's formula uses only the three side lengths — no height needed!

Heron's Formula:

For a triangle with sides a, b, and c:

  1. First calculate the semi-perimeter (half the perimeter):

\[

s = \frac{a + b + c}{2}

\]

  1. Then the area is:

\[

\text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}

\]

When to Use Heron's Formula:

  • When you know all three sides of a triangle
  • When you don't know the height
  • Especially useful for scalene triangles (all sides different)
  • Works for all types of triangles: acute, obtuse, right, isosceles, equilateral

Example Calculation:

Triangle with sides 5 cm, 12 cm, 13 cm (right triangle):

  • s = (5 + 12 + 13)/2 = 30/2 = 15 cm
  • Area = √[15(15-5)(15-12)(15-13)] = √[15 × 10 × 3 × 2] = √900 = 30 cm²

topics.title: Equilateral and Isosceles Triangles
topics.concept:
Where is Heron's Formula Used in Real Life?

Heron's formula has many practical applications beyond textbook problems. Any situation where you need to find the area of a triangular region and you can measure the sides (but not the height) is a candidate.

Real-Life Applications:

ApplicationDescription
**Construction**Calculating material needed for triangular roof sections, trusses, or gables
**Agriculture**Determining area of triangular fields for irrigation or crop planning
**Navigation**Triangulation for position finding and mapping
**Sports Fields**Calculating areas of triangular sections in grounds
**Art and Design**Finding area of triangular shapes in artwork or patterns

Why Heron's Formula is Practical:

  • You can measure side lengths directly with a tape measure
  • You may not be able to measure height (e.g., in a sloped field)
  • The formula works even if the triangle is not right-angled
  • It's simple enough to use with calculators or computers

Important Considerations:

  • All measurements must be in the same units
  • For very large areas, use appropriate units (square meters, square kilometers, acres)
  • Accuracy of measurements affects the accuracy of the area

quiz.q: The perimeter of a rhombus is 32 cm and its corresponding height is 5 cm. Its area is:
quiz.explanation: Side of the rhombus = 32 / 4 = 8 cm. Area = base × height = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

topics.title: Areas of Quadrilaterals
topics.concept:
A quadrilateral's area is found by a diagonal that splits it into two triangles; find each triangle's area (Heron's formula or ½ base × height) and add them.

This is the standard method for plots of land, parks and fields where four side lengths and a diagonal are measured.

examples.problem: A quadrilateral is split by a diagonal into triangles of area 12 and 18. Total?
Why split a quadrilateral by a diagonal?
examples.solution: To reduce it to two triangles whose areas can be found and added.

recap: Split a quadrilateral along a diagonal into two triangles.
Add the two triangle areas for the total.

quiz.q: Meena makes an umbrella by stitching 10 triangular pieces of cloth of two different colours. Each piece has sides 20 cm, 50 cm, and 50 cm. The total cloth required is:
quiz.explanation: s = 60 cm. Area of one piece = √(60 × 40 × 10 × 10) = 200√6 cm². Total cloth = 10 × 200√6 = 2000√6 cm².

questions.q: The sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 12 cm, and 13 cm. The altitude drawn on the longest side is:
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 cm². Also, ½ × 13 × altitude = 30 → altitude = 60/13 cm.

questions.q: If each side of a triangle is increased by 100%, the percentage increase in its area is:
questions.explanation: Increasing by 100% means the sides are doubled. New area = 4 × Original Area. Increase = 4A − A = 3A, which is 300%.

questions.q: Find the area of a triangle with sides 11 cm, 60 cm, and 61 cm.
questions.explanation: These sides form a right triangle (11² + 60² = 121 + 3600 = 3721 = 61²). Area = ½ × 11 × 60 = 330 cm². (Also verifiable via Heron's: s=66, Area = √(66×55×6×5) = 330).

questions.explanation: Total area = 576√6 cm². Cost in Rupees = 576√6 × 0.50 = ₹288√6.

questions.q: A quadrilateral park ABCD has AB = 9 m, BC = 12 m, CD = 5 m, DA = 8 m and angle C = 90°. Its total area is:
questions.explanation: Join BD. In right ΔBCD, BD = √(12² + 5²) = 13 m. Area BCD = ½ × 12 × 5 = 30 m². For ΔABD (sides 9, 8, 13), s = 15. Area = √(15 × 6 × 7 × 2) = 6√35 m². Total = 30 + 6√35 m².

questions.explanation: The right triangle (7, 24) has diagonal = √(7²+24²) = 25 cm and area = 84 cm². The second triangle has sides 15, 20, 25 (which is also a right triangle), area = 150 cm². Total = 234 cm².

questions.q: A triangular plot with sides 18 m, 24 m, and 30 m needs clearing. If the contractor charges ₹10 per m², what is the total bill?
questions.explanation: The sides form a right triangle (18, 24, 30 are a multiple of 3, 4, 5). Area = ½ × 18 × 24 = 216 m². Bill = 216 × 10 = ₹2160.

questions.q: If every side of a triangle is doubled, the ratio of the area of the original triangle to the new triangle is:
questions.explanation: When sides are doubled, the semi-perimeter doubles, making each (s-a) term double. √(2s × 2(s-a) × 2(s-b) × 2(s-c)) = √16 × Area = 4 × Area. Ratio is 1:4.

questions.q: The area of a triangle is calculated using base = 12 cm and height = 8 cm. If calculated correctly using Heron's formula with its three side lengths, the result will be:
questions.explanation: Both methods yield the exact same area. Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm².

questions.q: Calculate the area of quadrilateral ABCD where AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm, CD = 5 cm, DA = 5 cm, and AC = 5 cm.
questions.explanation: ΔABC is a right triangle (3,4,5), area = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6. ΔACD has sides 5, 5, 5 (equilateral), area = (√3/4) × 5² = 25√3/4. Total = 6 + 25√3/4 cm².
